narrative.intro: Haskell reported $262M in federal contract obligations in FY2026 to date, from 9 awards with an average award size of $29.1M, and obligations were up 582.4% year over year. FY2026 obligations of $262M exceed each prior fiscal year listed, including $38.3M in FY25 and $33.4M in FY24. The Department of Homeland Security is the largest buyer, accounting for $226M of obligations, followed by the Department of Defense at $35.8M. Commercial and Institutional Building Construction is the dominant market, with $262M in obligations, while Engineering Services accounts for $5K. Current-year totals are partial and represent fiscal year to date activity. These figures are contract obligations except where tables list total contract values for largest-awards and expiring-contracts. The concentration of obligations in one market and one buyer is notable: Commercial and Institutional Building Construction and the Department of Homeland Security together represent the majority of FY2026 obligations.

sections.heading: How concentrated are Haskell's FY2026 obligations?
sections.body: The Department of Homeland Security accounts for $226M of Haskell's FY2026 obligations, making DHS the dominant buyer. Commercial and Institutional Building Construction accounts for $262M, which equals total FY2026 obligations, indicating strong concentration in one market. The Department of Defense contributed $35.8M, the only other buyer listed. Engineering Services shows $5K, signaling minimal activity outside the primary market.

sections.heading: How do FY2026 obligations compare with prior years?
sections.body: FY2026 obligations are $262M, larger than any prior year listed: $38.3M in FY25, $33.4M in FY24, $57.5M in FY23, $54.6M in FY22, and $34.3M in FY21. Obligations rose up 582.4% year over year. The company received 9 awards in FY2026 to date with an average award size of $29.1M. Current-year totals are partial and fiscal year to date.

faq.q: How much does Haskell make from federal contracts?
faq.a: Haskell has $262M in federal contract obligations in FY2026 to date. The company received 9 awards this fiscal year to date with an average award size of $29.1M, and obligations were up 582.4% year over year.

The Department of Homeland Security and the Department of Defense buy from Haskell. The Department of Homeland Security accounts for $226M in obligations and the Department of Defense accounts for $35.8M.

faq.q: What does Haskell sell to the government?
faq.a: Haskell sells work in Commercial and Institutional Building Construction and Engineering Services to the government. Commercial and Institutional Building Construction accounts for $262M in obligations and Engineering Services accounts for $5K.
